0 · What changed

From the approved mock to today

  1. The tour had its own page (release 59); release 61 folded it into the guide as a map column. [R]
  2. The stop cards went with it, so no stop shows its photo now. Haro's station is gone from the tour. [V]
  3. The map shrank from 61% of the screen width to 46%. [V]
  4. The black card by the pin (one sentence and its source) is gone; a stop is now a link line under the text. [V]
  5. Release 62 moves the map each time a stop link crosses the reading line, so it flies mid-section. In my stop 1 capture the map still showed all of northern Spain. [V]

The weather

Cool in the west, warm in the east

The whole valley sits where the Atlantic and the Mediterranean meet, so temperatures stay mild and about 400 mm of rain falls in a year.

Moving east, the climate turns Mediterranean and the wine changes with it.

Rioja AltaRioja AlavesaRioja Oriental

Rioja Alta. Atlantic. More rain and fewer hours of sun than the south.

A, plus "Fly the tour"

  1. The guide keeps the calm map from A.
  2. The top of the guide gets a big Fly the tour button with a photo.
  3. The map band keeps a small Fly the tour too.
  4. It opens the approved tour again, as you signed it off in release 59.
  5. One chapter on screen at a time.
  6. A big pitched map.
  7. A photo in every stop card.
  8. Slow flights: 2.5 to 4 s, two legs for long hops, a 2.2 s pause between stops.
Why this one
  1. It brings back the exact cinematic tour you approved, not a new guess at it.
  2. The tour code from release 59 is in git, so this is a restore more than a build. [R]
  3. The guide stays the default and stays readable.
  4. Its map stops jumping (A).

What the rules make

Made for the barrel

Rioja makes sparkling wine too. Wines "made by the Champagne method" from Rioja Alta and Alavesa were shown in Madrid in 1857, and in 1890 a French firm in Haro's station quarter hired a champagne maker from Reims.

Haro's station quarter

The cool end of the Winkler heat scale keeps the base wines fresh and acidic. Since 2017 the rules cover traditional-method sparkling whites and rosés.

Cinematic inside the guide

  1. Open the tour and the map goes full-bleed behind the guide.
  2. The guide's own text scrolls as cards over the map, one stop per card.
  3. Each card carries its stop photo; the map flies slowly between cards.
  4. After the last stop the map slides away and the full guide continues below.

For you to decide

  1. Decided (owner 21 Oct): B. The guide stays the default, with a big Fly the tour button and a photo at the top.
  2. Still open: D, a full-bleed version, only if you reopen it.
  3. The approved mock was a text column beside a 61% map, not full-bleed. D would be new; B is what you signed off.
  4. Stops with no photo of their own (the overview, the climate start, the barrel start): show no card, or the section photo?
  5. Photos here use a CSS focus only. Shipped crops still need their crop sheet check.
  6. The live stop 1 capture kept the map on northern Spain. Worth a bug check whichever option you pick.
